_note: Running an agent for real: how chkm8 is separated from r3lik. Rendered in A4 #notes and by the console `setup` command. Public facts only: no account numbers, addresses of servers, or key locations beyond 'Keychain'.

items.d: r3lik set up a separate account for everything it touches, and it is never signed in to his.
Logins, cards and 2FA codes are filled from a vault, so they never enter the conversation. Keys live in the Keychain or the cluster and are read by code, never printed.

Trading, monitoring and reports run on a single-node k3s server in Nuremberg, and orders are signed only there. The agent and its terminal live on a MacBook Air in Los Angeles that holds no exchange key.
The Kubernetes API isn't on the internet. kubectl goes through an SSH tunnel with key-only login, and the firewall lets in SSH and nothing else.
Commits are made as chkm8 and co-authored by r3lik. Private values are stripped before anything reaches GitHub, and every push is scanned for leaks.
He designed these boundaries. He decides the caps, which accounts it may use and what it may post, and can pause new trades at any time.
